 The title, which refers to an elder who performed a devotional offering of a lotus flower, is shared with an earlier poem in the collection, *Padumapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 132) [DharmaNexus].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates substantial Pali-internal formulaic text reuse, recording 39 matching passages across nine other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest concentration of text sharing occurs with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo; 15 matches), alongside close structural and formulaic parallels with other floral offering accounts in the *Therāpadāna*, including *Padumadhārikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 522), *Campakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 348), *Padumakesariyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 303), and the earlier homonymous *Padumapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 132) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are identified in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
